effect: Epicurus's argument concerns the experience of being dead, not painful dying or grief; I can now connect it to his account of a sufficient life.
reaction: That distinction makes the argument clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Epicurus's argument against fearing death was most worthwhile: distinguishing being dead from painful dying and grief made its claim precise.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final Stoic combination felt least developed; it stated the extension of concern without much exploration.

surprise.text: The warning that voluntary simplicity does not make forced poverty harmless added an important qualification to Diogenes's self-sufficiency.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the final combination was the only available choice.

continue.text: I would consider continuing: the distinctions around death, poverty and pleasure made the ideas useful, though I would hope for more developed choices.
